column1: # Hand labels for test-video3. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
# Frame numbers are the ones burned into label-part-A.mp4 and label-part-B.mp4.
#   label-part-A.mp4   frames 0-2500, at a third speed   (128 s to watch)
#   label-part-B.mp4   frames 2450-5030, at full speed   (44 s to watch)
# The two parts overlap by 50 frames on purpose, so nothing falls down the join.
# Both are the working video with a frame number burned on and nothing else: no boxes,
# no hit markers, no rally spans, no predictions. Label the whole clip, both parts.
# This clip is a phone recording of a broadcast, so it is letterboxed and carries a
# Subscribe overlay. The court sits inside the black bars; frame numbers still refer to
# the working video and are what every label means.
# ONE LINE PER RACKET CONTACT
#     c  <frame>  <near|far|?>  [shot]  [note...]
#   frame   where the racket meets the shuttle. Within 3 or 4 frames is fine; the scorer
#           matches a prediction to a contact within 0.2 s, which is 12 frames here.
#   near    the player on this side of the net, nearer the camera.
#   far     the player beyond the net.
#   ?       you could not tell who hit it. Use it freely -- a contact with no hitter is
#           still scored for detection and is simply left out of the hitter figure, which
#           is better than a guess.
# ONE LINE PER CONTACT THAT IS REAL BUT NOT A RALLY SHOT
#     k  <frame>  <near|far|?>  [shot]  [note...]
#   Handing the shuttle back, a knock-up between points, a player bouncing it on their
#   racket. Real contacts, but not part of a rally, and scored as neither hit nor miss.
# ONE LINE PER RALLY
#     r  <start_frame>  <end_frame>  [note...]
#   Start at the serve contact. End where the shuttle comes to rest or play plainly stops.
#   Include every rally you see in either part of the video.
# THE SHOT FIELD IS OPTIONAL and is for the next milestone, not this one.
# If you want to save yourself watching this clip a second time later, add one of:
#     smash  drop  clear  lift  drive  net  serve  other  uncertain
# straight after the hitter. Nothing in the current scoring reads it. Leave it off and
# nothing is lost from this task.
# Example of the format, not of this clip:
#     c 120 near serve
#     c 151 far lift
#     c 188 near smash
#     k 940 near        returning the shuttle to the server
c 9 near lift
c 82 far smash
c 109 near net shot doesnt go over
c 765 far serve
c 811 near lift
c 884 far clear backhand
c 960 near smash
c 1570 near serve
c 1621 far net
c 1673 near lift
# CORRECTION, 15 Sep 2026, agreed with the labeller.
# The lines "c 1605 far net" and "c 1636 far smash" were two entries for one contact and
# neither sat on it. The raw track descends steadily through 1605 with no reversal, turns
# over at 1620-1623, and at 1637 loses two thirds of its speed across the turn, which is the
# signature of an apex rather than a racket. Frames 1616-1627 show the far player lunging at
# the net with the shuttle at his racket. Recorded as one contact at 1621, keeping the
# labeller's hitter and shot type. Without this the rally read far, far in succession.
# RALLY SPANS. Derived, not watched: the labeller recorded contacts, and these spans were
# read off the raw shuttle track afterwards by one rule -- start at the serve contact, end
# where the shuttle comes to rest. They are weaker evidence than the contacts above.
# rally 1 is truncated by the start of the clip: the first contact is at frame 9 and the
#   rally was already in progress, so it starts at 0 as clip 2's first rally does. The
#   shuttle is still at 124-132 after the net shot at 109 that did not go over.
# rally 2 ends with the smash at 960. TrackNet loses the shuttle for five frames immediately
#   after it, which is what a smash does to it, and the track is unreliable from about 1000;
#   985 is the landing read from the descent at 968-996.
# rally 3 ends with the lift at 1673, which rises to an apex at about 1705 and descends to
#   y 0.83 -- the near court floor -- by 1776.
# The labeller reports that the remainder of the clip is a half-time break with no rallies,
# which is why no span covers it.
